channel.title: Use & Like: app news
channel.description: What changed in the apps you use, in our own words, with what it means for you and what to do about it.

item.title: GTA 6 cloud gaming explained: Xbox One, PC, Remote Play and size
item.description: GTA 6 came out on 19 November for PS5 and Xbox Series X and S, Xbox One owners can only stream it through Xbox Cloud Gaming, there's no PC version or PC streaming, and Remote Play lets you stream it from your own console to another screen.

item.title: Is it safe to charge your phone at the airport? Juice jacking explained
item.description: Charging from an airport USB port carries a small risk known as juice jacking, where a rigged port tries to reach your phone's data, but security researchers know of no credible real attacks, and your own charger or a battery pack takes the risk away.

item.title: Streaming bundles 2026 explained: Disney+ Hulu app, HBO Max, Fubo
item.description: Streaming services are folding into each other: Hulu's live TV moves into the Disney+ app in December, Paramount+ and HBO Max are due as one bundle in early 2027, and Fubo now adds Disney+ and Hulu to two of its plans at no extra cost.

item.title: Android sideloading verification goes worldwide from January 2027
item.description: Google will start requiring a verified developer for Android apps installed from outside the Play Store in every region from January 2027, Ars Technica reports, with the rollout to all devices taking several months. Until now the rule applied only in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand, where it began on 30 September 2026.

item.title: AVANT CAMERA is a cinematic video camera app for iPhone
item.description: AVANT CAMERA adds film-style colour to your videos while you record, so you see the look before you edit. It was #88 among paid Photo & Video apps on the US App Store on 19 November.

item.title: Black Friday scams 2026: fake shops, delivery texts and fake numbers
item.description: The Black Friday scams warned about this month copy real shops, carriers and customer service lines, and going straight to the shop's own app or website and paying by credit card protects against most of them.

item.title: Canva turn off AI features: new switch for free and paid users
item.description: Canva now has a setting that switches off its generative AI tools, such as Magic Expand (which extends a photo), Magic Write and image making in its chatbot. It's there for free and paid accounts, with a second option to see less AI-made content in the library.

item.title: FernShift shift calendar app for iPhone plans rotating work shifts
item.description: FernShift is a 2.99 dollar iPhone and iPad calendar for people who work rotating shifts, with repeating patterns of up to eight weeks and 12-hour or 8-hour schedules. It was #87 among paid Productivity apps on the US App Store on 19 November.

item.title: Gemini for Mac computer use: it now works your apps in the background
item.description: The Gemini app for Mac can now click, type and fill in forms across your Mac's apps, files and websites to finish a task you describe. It's rolling out from 19 November in the US, in English, for Google AI Plus, Pro and Ultra subscribers.

item.title: Google homepage redesign: Gemini sidebar with your chats on desktop
item.description: The Google Search homepage on computers is getting Gemini shortcuts under the search bar for making images, analysing files and brainstorming, in place of the Google Search button. A new sidebar lists your Gemini chats and tasks with a New chat button.

item.title: Halide camera app on iPhone Duo: bigger viewfinder and fill flash
item.description: Halide 3.4, out on 19 November, adds an XL viewfinder for the iPhone Duo when it's open, and can turn the outer screen into a live preview for the person you photograph or into a soft fill light.

item.title: HeyGen Avatar 6: make an AI avatar video of yourself from a photo
item.description: HeyGen launched Avatar 6, a model that turns one photo of you and a short recording of your voice into a video of you reading a script. It makes 2K video, matches hand gestures to what you say and can put two avatars in one conversation.

item.title: IconSwapper Mac app shows your ChatGPT and Claude usage on Dock icons
item.description: IconSwapper is a new Mac app that changes the icons in your Dock, including live icons that show how much of your ChatGPT, Claude or Cursor allowance you've used and when it resets. It costs 19 dollars once at launch, later 29 dollars.

item.title: LoopListen: shadowing app for iPhone loops a phrase until you get it
item.description: LoopListen is a 99-cent iPhone and iPad app for listening practice: tap A and B to mark a part of a recording, and it repeats that part with pauses so you can say it back. It was #69 among paid Education apps on the US App Store on 19 November.

item.title: Meta Muse Charm price may be 300 dollars with free Verizon 5G
item.description: Meta plans to sell its Muse Charm, a pocket device for talking to its Muse AI agent, for 300 dollars with up to 12 months of free Verizon 5G data, according to The Information, citing one person familiar with the plans. Meta hasn't confirmed the price or the Verizon offer.

item.title: MoodyRoutine brings Samsung-style Modes and Routines to Pixel phones
item.description: MoodyRoutine is a free Android app that copies the idea of Samsung's Modes and Routines for other phones such as Google Pixels: modes like Sleep or Exercise switch on by time or when headphones connect and change your settings.

item.title: OpenAI phone: Foxconn unit reportedly got an order to build it
item.description: China's Securities Times reports that FIH Mobile, part of iPhone assembler Foxconn, has an order to help build a smartphone for ChatGPT maker OpenAI. The report cites unnamed supply chain sources, and OpenAI hasn't confirmed any phone.

item.title: Passkeys vs passwords explained: how they work on iPhone and Android
item.description: A passkey lets you sign in with your face, fingerprint or phone PIN instead of a password, and because it never leaves your device as a secret you could type in, a fake website can't trick you into handing it over.

item.title: Phone overheating with CarPlay or Android Auto: why and what helps
item.description: A phone running CarPlay or Android Auto often does several heavy jobs at once (navigation, music, mobile data and charging) in a warm car, and Apple and Google both say long navigation sessions, sunlight and hot cars make phones heat up, so a cable, a shaded spot and a lighter load usually help.

item.title: Play That Back camera app: film with live looks on iPhone and Duo
item.description: Play That Back is a new free camera app for iPhone and iPad that shows a colour look live while you film and keeps a clean original of every shot. On the iPhone Duo, the person you're filming sees the look on the outer screen and can pick it.

item.title: Proton Drive import from Google Drive: Easy Switch moves your files
item.description: Proton Drive can now import your Google Drive files and folders through Easy Switch on the web, keeping your folder structure. It's for all plans and rolling out gradually.

item.title: Raylie flight view app shows which side of the plane to sit on
item.description: Raylie is a free iPhone app that turns a boarding pass into a timeline of what you'll see from the window, from sunrise to cities below, and on which side. It was #96 among free Travel apps on the US App Store on 19 November.

item.title: Running app without subscription: echoRnr costs $9.99 once
item.description: echoRnr is a running app you buy once, with no ads and no monthly fee, and it lets you race a past run of your own or a friend's in real time. It came out on 19 November and was #18 among paid Health & Fitness apps on the US App Store the same day.

item.title: Samsung Android laptop leak: 14- and 16-inch 'Origin' models
item.description: Code in the One UI 9.5 beta points to two Samsung laptops running Android, codenamed Origin, in 14- and 16-inch sizes with Qualcomm's Snapdragon X Elite chip, Android Authority found. Samsung hasn't announced an Android laptop.

item.title: Samsung Galaxy Studio headphones leak: 870mAh battery and 3.5mm jack
item.description: Samsung's unannounced Galaxy Studio over-ear headphones may have an 870mAh battery and a 3.5mm headphone jack next to USB-C, according to One UI 9.5 beta code found by SammyGuru and reported by Android Authority. Samsung hasn't confirmed them.

item.title: Samsung Open Gate video and 360 panorama may come with One UI 9.5
item.description: Code in the One UI 9.5 beta's Camera app points to Open Gate video, which records with the whole camera sensor, and a Dual cam panorama that uses the front and rear cameras for up to 360 degrees, Android Authority found. Samsung hasn't announced either, and neither works in the beta.

item.title: Surfshark scam call protection comes to the iPhone app
item.description: Surfshark's iPhone app now has Call protection, which filters spam and possible scam calls in real time. It came with version 5.3.0 on 19 November and, according to TechRadar, needs a premium Surfshark plan.

item.title: Tromsø northern lights app made by local aurora guides
item.description: Guide To Tromsø is an iPhone and iPad app for the northern lights in Tromsø, Norway, made by local aurora guides: it shows live aurora data, a cloud map, recent sightings from other users and viewing spots. It costs 49 cents once, with no subscription, and was #96 among paid Travel apps on the US App Store on 19 November.

item.title: Turn burst photos into video with BurstReel on iPhone and Mac
item.description: BurstReel makes a short video out of a burst of photos, with a pace you set from 1 to 60 photos a second. It was #92 among paid Photo & Video apps on the US App Store on 19 November.

item.title: TV Jr. app puts your HDHomeRun live TV channels on iPhone
item.description: TV Jr. is a new 1.99-dollar iPhone app that lays out live TV you already have, from an HDHomeRun antenna tuner, your own playlists or streams, as a simple channel list that also works on HomeView. It brings no channels of its own and was #9 among paid Entertainment apps on the US App Store on 19 November.

item.title: Upp NFC alarm clock app for iPhone only stops when you scan a tag
item.description: Upp is a 99-cent iPhone alarm clock that keeps ringing until you scan an NFC sticker you've placed somewhere else, like the coffee machine or the bathroom mirror. It was #82 among paid Productivity apps on the US App Store on 19 November.

item.title: VHS camcorder app for iPhone records retro 90s video looks
item.description: VHS Camcorder: 90s Retro Cam turns the iPhone into six old cameras, from a 1994 VHS camcorder and a 2004 Mini DV to Super 8 film, night vision and a CCTV deck, for a one-time $4.99. It was #43 among paid Photo & Video apps on the US App Store on 19 November.

item.title: WhatsApp group limit increase: groups now hold up to 1,500 members
item.description: WhatsApp is raising the maximum group size from 1,024 to 1,500 members on Android and iPhone, for regular groups and the group chats inside Communities. It's rolling out gradually on the latest app versions, so only some accounts have it so far.

item.title: YourTrackPal GPS fitness tracker app: 10 sports, no subscription
item.description: YourTrackPal is a $1.99 GPS workout tracker for iPhone that covers ten sports, from running and cycling to swimming and skiing, with no subscription, ads or account. It was #66 among paid Health & Fitness apps on the US App Store on 19 November.

item.title: ChatGPT ads on Free and Go plans: what they look like and who sees them
item.description: ChatGPT shows ads to people on its Free plan and the $8-a-month Go plan, now in 89 countries, while Plus, Pro and Enterprise stay ad-free. An Android Police writer says the ads now show up after nearly every reply on Go.

item.title: Google AI Ultra now includes YouTube Premium Family for 5 members
item.description: Google AI Ultra subscribers now get YouTube Premium Family, which covers up to five family members in one household, instead of the Individual plan. It applies to Ultra 5x at 99.99 dollars a month and Ultra 20x at 199.99 dollars a month.

item.title: Affiliate links on Instagram Reels and YouTube explained
item.description: An affiliate link pays the creator a commission when you buy through it, and since 16 November US creators can put Amazon affiliate links right into Instagram Reels and feed posts, as YouTube creators already can with tagged products.

item.title: AI Photo Edit: online AI photo editor that works from one sentence
item.description: AI Photo Edit is a web photo editor where you upload a picture, type the change you want, and it redraws only that part. It can swap outfits or backgrounds, remove people or text and restore old prints.

item.title: Alfred 6 for Mac: new features, query history and Alfred UI
item.description: Alfred 6, the Mac app launcher from Running with Crayons, came out on 18 November with Query History, a longer Clipboard History and Alfred UI, a toolkit that lets workflows show their own windows and controls.

item.title: App Store Awards 2026 finalists: 45 apps and games picked by Apple
item.description: Apple named 45 finalists for its 2026 App Store Awards across iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, Vision Pro and Apple Arcade, plus a Cultural Impact group. The iPhone App of the Year finalists are ElevenReader, (Not Boring) Camera and Raylie.

item.title: Audible AI features: audio discovery, recaps and Ask a Question in the US
item.description: Audible is rolling out audio discovery in the US, short clips that mix an AI overview of a book, comments from its author or an Audible editor and a narrated sample, starting with select English titles. Recaps and Ask a Question, which were in beta, reach more US titles now and roll out widely from December.

item.title: Banking app security issues: half of 2,686 apps had serious flaws
item.description: Security firm Ostorlab tested 2,686 mobile banking apps from 487 banks in 64 countries and found that 51.5% had at least one high or critical security problem. Its scanner got past the fingerprint or face login in 35.1% of the Android apps.

item.title: Bitwarden passkey manager now works natively in Windows 11 and macOS
item.description: Bitwarden's desktop app can now be set as the passkey provider in Windows 11 and macOS, so the system's own passkey window saves and uses passkeys from your Bitwarden vault. It works in websites without the browser extension.

item.title: BugMeNot shut down after more than 20 years
item.description: BugMeNot, the site where people shared logins for websites that force you to register, has closed. Its homepage now only says it has closed and thanks everyone who envisioned a better internet; no reason was given.

item.title: ChatGPT dictation time limit removed with new Live Dictation
item.description: ChatGPT's dictation now writes your words on screen while you're still speaking, and the old 10-minute recording limit is gone. OpenAI is rolling it out on all plans, free included, on iPhone, Android, the web and the desktop app.

item.title: Connecticut Mobile ID app: your driver's license on your phone
item.description: Connecticut's free Mobile ID app puts your driver's license, learner's permit or state ID on your phone from 18 November. The TSA accepts it at participating airport checkpoints, but police and polling places don't.

item.title: Daybreak exports Apple Health data to CSV and JSON files
item.description: Daybreak is a new $0.99 iPhone and iPad app that copies up to 80 daily Apple Health metrics into CSV and JSON files in a folder you pick. It was #80 among paid Health & Fitness apps on the US App Store on 18 November.

item.title: DirecTV Netflix, HBO Max and Apple TV bundle from $27.99 a month
item.description: DirecTV streaming customers can now get Netflix, HBO Max and Apple TV in one monthly bundle. The Value plan costs $27.99 plus tax with ads on Netflix and HBO Max; Deluxe costs $43.49 plus tax without them.

item.title: Flood Atlas: free South Florida flood map app with alerts and routes
item.description: Flood Atlas is a free iPhone app that puts National Weather Service flood alerts, NOAA tide and river gauges and neighbours' flooded-street reports for South Florida on one map. It was #39 among free Weather apps on the US App Store on 18 November.

item.title: Foldwriter typewriter app: a half-folded iPhone Duo types letters
item.description: Foldwriter is a $1.99 app that shows paper on the top half of a half-folded iPhone Duo and typewriter keys below, with clacking keys and a margin bell. It was #51 among paid Entertainment apps on the US App Store on 18 November.
